intro: Wet rooms have become one of the most sought-after bathroom upgrades in Stockport over the last decade, and it's easy to see why. They offer a clean, accessible, and genuinely luxurious alternative to a traditional shower enclosure or bath setup — and when installed properly, they add real value to a home. But getting one right isn't straightforward. It requires careful waterproofing, precise drainage design, and an understanding of the building fabric you're working with. Get any of those wrong and you're looking at water damage, damp, and costly remedial work. This guide explains what's involved, what it costs in Stockport, and what to look out for when choosing a local installer.
localContext: Stockport's housing stock is more varied than many people realise, and that variation matters enormously for wet room installations. Edwardian semis — common throughout areas like Heaton Moor, Davenport, and Heaviley — typically have solid or suspended timber floors, which need specialist attention before any wet room can be installed. Timber floors require a marine-ply build-up, additional membrane layers, and sometimes structural reinforcement to handle a linear drain and tile weight. Post-war estates across areas like Bredbury and Offerton are more likely to have solid concrete floors, which makes the tanking process more straightforward but can present challenges with headroom in bathrooms that were designed conservatively. Newer developments in Stockport town centre and surrounding areas tend to have modern screed floors that adapt well to wet room drainage. Stockport also sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale can build up on glass, tiles, and fittings over time. It's worth factoring in a quality water softener or at least a scale-inhibiting shower head when planning your wet room, otherwise you'll be fighting a losing battle with cleaning and maintenance.
serviceDetail: A proper wet room installation in Stockport follows a clear sequence of work, and any reputable installer will follow each stage methodically. The first step is a survey of the existing bathroom — assessing the floor construction, wall condition, drainage run positions, and whether the existing waste pipe can accommodate a linear or centre drain. This survey shapes everything that follows. Next comes the strip-out: removing the old suite, wall coverings, and floor finish down to the base structure. Once the room is back to its shell, the waterproofing begins. This is the most critical stage. A tanking system — typically a combination of liquid membrane and reinforced fabric tape — is applied to the floor and all walls to at least 1.8 metres, sometimes full height. Getting this stage wrong is what causes most wet room failures, so it's not a place to cut corners. The drainage channel or point drain is then set into the floor, with the floor itself graded — usually at a 1 in 80 fall — to direct water cleanly to the outlet. After tanking, the floor and walls are tiled, with particular attention to grout joint sizing and tile choice for slip resistance. Finally, the shower valve, screen if required, and all other fittings are installed and connected. From start to finish, most Stockport wet rooms take between five and ten days depending on scope and any structural surprises.
pricing: Wet room installation in Stockport typically costs between £6,000 and £12,000 for a full conversion, including labour, waterproofing, drainage, tiling, and a quality shower valve and fittings. The lower end of that range applies to smaller bathrooms with concrete floors and straightforward drainage routes. Edwardian semis with timber floors will usually sit in the £8,000 to £10,000 bracket once the additional floor preparation is accounted for. High-end finishes — large format porcelain tiles, designer drains, rainfall showers, and bespoke glass screens — can push costs beyond £12,000. It's worth getting at least two or three detailed quotes from Stockport-based installers who have actually surveyed the room rather than quoting blind.
whyLocal: Choosing a Stockport-based installer rather than a national firm or someone travelling from further afield makes a genuine practical difference. A local tradesperson will have worked on the types of properties common in the area — they'll know the challenges of Edwardian timber floors, the quirks of older drainage systems, and the building regulations that apply in the Stockport Metropolitan Borough. They're also much easier to get back if a snag appears after completion. Reputation matters locally in a way it simply doesn't for a company operating across a wide region. Ask for examples of completed wet rooms in Stockport specifically, and check reviews that mention the town by name.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an Edwardian semi in Stockport with a timber floor?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires more preparation than a concrete floor. The timber subfloor needs to be assessed for structural integrity, reinforced if necessary, and built up with moisture-resistant ply before tanking. It adds cost and time but is entirely achievable. Most experienced Stockport bathroom installers have done this many times in properties across Heaton Moor and similar areas.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Stockport?
faqs.a: Most wet rooms in Stockport take between five and ten working days from strip-out to final fit-off. Smaller rooms with straightforward concrete floors sit at the lower end. Larger bathrooms, complex tiling, or older properties requiring floor remediation can take closer to two weeks. Your installer should give you a realistic timeline after surveying the room.

faqs.q: Will hard water in Stockport cause problems with my wet room?
faqs.a: Stockport's moderately hard water supply does mean limescale will accumulate on tiles, glass screens, and shower fittings over time. It won't damage the installation structurally, but it does affect appearance and requires regular cleaning. Fitting a scale-inhibiting device to the shower supply, or choosing textured tiles and matt fittings that hide deposits more easily, are practical ways to manage this.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission or building regulations approval for a wet room in Stockport?
faqs.a: Planning permission isn't usually required for an internal bathroom conversion. However, if the work involves alterations to drainage or significant structural changes, Building Regulations may apply — particularly around ventilation requirements and waterproofing standards. A competent Stockport installer should advise you on this during the survey and handle any necessary notifications to Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council on your behalf.
